# FRAMEWORK data dictionary

<!-- Generated by `python -m app.schema_doc` from the schema definitions in code. Do not edit it:
     change the schema (with its migration in app/migrate.py), then run the command.
     tests/test_schema_doc.py fails while this file is out of date. -->

Every store is a SQLite file in `reader/data/`, which is gitignored: a fresh clone has none, and each is created by the build named below. The schema version is the store's `PRAGMA user_version`; `python -m app.migrate --status` reports it for the stores on disk, and `app/migrate.py` holds the numbered migrations that bring an older store forward.

| Store | File | Schema version | Tables |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| [CFR title](#cfr-title-title-nsqlite3) | `title-{N}.sqlite3` | 1 | `meta`, `sections`, `front_matter`, `sections_fts`, `title_graph` |
| [U.S. Code title](#us-code-title-usc-nsqlite3) | `usc-{N}.sqlite3` | 1 | `meta`, `sections`, `notes`, `sections_fts`, `notes_fts` |
| [Federal Register](#federal-register-frsqlite3) | `fr.sqlite3` | 1 | `meta`, `documents`, `document_bodies`, `document_cfr`, `coverage`, `build_chunks`, `documents_fts` |
| [Newsroom](#newsroom-osha_newssqlite3) | `osha_news.sqlite3` | 4 | `articles`, `article_citations`, `articles_fts`, `sync_status`, `enforcement_cases`, `enforcement_narratives_fts`, `dol_datasets`, `fr_bodies` |
| [U.S. Constitution](#us-constitution-constitutionsqlite3) | `constitution.sqlite3` | 1 | `meta`, `units`, `notes`, `units_fts`, `notes_fts` |
| [Public Laws](#public-laws-plawsqlite3) | `plaw.sqlite3` | 1 | `meta`, `laws`, `law_usc`, `build_chunks`, `laws_fts` |
| [Unified Agenda](#unified-agenda-agendasqlite3) | `agenda.sqlite3` | 1 | `meta`, `entries`, `editions`, `build_chunks`, `entries_fts` |
| [Source selection](#source-selection-sourcessqlite3) | `sources.sqlite3` | 1 | `settings`, `templates` |

Reading the tables below: **required** is `NOT NULL`; a column with no rule may be empty. Full-text (FTS5) tables are search indexes over another table, listed with the columns they index. Notes on columns are the comments written in the schema source.

## CFR title: `title-{N}.sqlite3`

One per installed CFR title: every section and appendix of the title (or of the parts chosen for a partial install), as eCFR XML and as plain text.

- **Built by:** `python -m app.build --title N`, or a Library download. A build replaces the whole file.
- **Written:** Replaced whole: a migration or reindex rewrites a copy and swaps it in.
- **Beside it:** `tree-{N}.json`, the title's contents tree, served to the sidebar as it is.
- **Schema version:** 1 (`migrate.latest("cfr")`)
- **Migrations:**
  - Version 1: Adopt schema versions; make sure the citation-graph table exists

### `meta`

Facts about the build, as key and value (keys below).

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `value` | TEXT |  |  |

### `sections`

One row per section or appendix, in reading order.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `kind` | TEXT | required | 'section' or 'appendix' |
| `ord` | INTEGER | required | reading order across the whole title |
| `part` | TEXT |  |  |
| `label` | TEXT | required | e.g. '§ 541.100' |
| `title` | TEXT | required | e.g. 'General rule for executive employees.' |
| `reserved` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `path` | TEXT | required | JSON breadcrumb of ancestors |
| `ecfr_path` | TEXT |  |  |
| `xml` | TEXT | required |  |
| `text` | TEXT | required |  |

- **Index** `sections_ord`: ord
- **Index** `sections_part`: part

### `front_matter`

Authority and source notes of parts and subparts, keyed `part/{N}` and `part/{N}/subpart/{X}`.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `xml` | TEXT | required |  |

### `sections_fts` (FTS5)

Full-text index over `sections` (`id` joins back to it).

- **Columns:** `id` (stored, not searched), `label`, `title`, `text`
- **tokenize:** `porter unicode61`

### `title_graph`

Derived: the title's citation graph as one JSON document under `key = 'index'` (web references, cited-by backlinks, IBR catalog). `python -m app.reindex` rebuilds it.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `payload` | TEXT | required |  |

### Meta keys (`meta`)

| Key | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `title` | The CFR title number. |
| `title_name` | The title's name, from eCFR. |
| `edition` | The eCFR edition date the text is from (`up_to_date_as_of`). |
| `built_at` | When the store was built (local time). |
| `fetched_at` | When the structure and text were downloaded (UTC). |
| `section_count` | Rows in `sections`. |
| `missing_leaves` | Structure entries that had no text in the XML. |
| `missing_sample` | JSON list of up to ten of those ids; present only when some are missing. |
| `scope` | JSON `{parts, sections}` of a partial install; absent for a whole title. |
| `source_url` | The eCFR full-text XML URL. |
| `structure_url` | The eCFR structure JSON URL. |
| `structure_sha256` | SHA-256 of the structure JSON in canonical form. |
| `xml_sha256` | SHA-256 of the downloaded XML, or of the piece manifest for a partial install. |
| `xml_sha256_kind` | `file` or `manifest`: what `xml_sha256` covers. |
| `xml_pieces` | JSON list of `{url, sha256}` per downloaded piece; partial installs only. |

## U.S. Code title: `usc-{N}.sqlite3`

One per installed U.S. Code title, from the OLRC's USLM XML. Appendix titles are numbered 100 + N (5a is `usc-105.sqlite3`).

- **Built by:** `python -m app.usc_build --title N`, or a Library download. A build replaces the whole file.
- **Written:** Replaced whole: a migration or reindex rewrites a copy and swaps it in.
- **Beside it:** `usc-tree-{N}.json`, the title's chapter outline.
- **Schema version:** 1 (`migrate.latest("usc")`)
- **Migrations:**
  - Version 1: Adopt schema versions

### `meta`

Facts about the build, as key and value (keys below).

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `value` | TEXT |  |  |

### `sections`

One row per section, in reading order; `status` is NULL for a section in force.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `identifier` | TEXT |  |  |
| `kind` | TEXT | required |  |
| `ord` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `chapter` | TEXT |  |  |
| `label` | TEXT | required |  |
| `heading` | TEXT | required |  |
| `path` | TEXT | required |  |
| `status` | TEXT |  |  |
| `xml` | TEXT | required |  |
| `text` | TEXT | required |  |
| `source_credit` | TEXT |  |  |

- **Index** `sections_chapter`: chapter
- **Index** `sections_ord`: ord

### `notes`

Editorial, statutory and executive notes, kept apart from the section text. `owner` is a section id or a level identifier such as `/us/usc/t4/ch1`.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | INTEGER | primary key |  |
| `owner` | TEXT | required |  |
| `owner_kind` | TEXT | required |  |
| `ord` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `category` | TEXT | required |  |
| `topic` | TEXT |  |  |
| `heading` | TEXT |  |  |
| `xml` | TEXT | required |  |
| `text` | TEXT | required |  |

- **Index** `notes_owner`: owner, ord

### `sections_fts` (FTS5)

Full-text index over `sections` (`id` joins back to it).

- **Columns:** `id` (stored, not searched), `label`, `heading`, `text`
- **tokenize:** `porter unicode61`

### `notes_fts` (FTS5)

Full-text index over `notes` (rowid = `notes.id`).

- **Columns:** `owner` (stored, not searched), `heading`, `text`
- **tokenize:** `porter unicode61`

### Meta keys (`meta`)

| Key | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `title` | The title number (100 + N for an appendix title). |
| `title_name` | The title's name. |
| `release_point` | The OLRC release point the text is from, such as `119-142`. |
| `current_through` | The public law the release point is current through. |
| `built_at` | When the store was built (UTC). |
| `section_count` | Rows in `sections`. |
| `note_count` | Rows in `notes`. |
| `duplicate_ids` | Sections whose number repeated and got a `~2` suffix. |
| `positive_law` | `1` when the title is enacted as positive law. |
| `publication` | The publication name in the XML's metadata. |
| `source_url` | The zip that was downloaded. |
| `release_page` | The OLRC page where the release point was found. |
| `zip_sha256` | SHA-256 of the zip. |
| `xml_sha256` | SHA-256 of the XML inside it. |
| `xml_member` | The XML file's name inside the zip. |

## Federal Register: `fr.sqlite3`

The Federal Register archive: one row per document inside the collected window, with full text fetched on demand.

- **Built by:** `python -m app.fr_build` (resumable; staged in `fr.sqlite3.tmp`), then updated in place.
- **Written:** Also written between builds: a migration runs in one transaction on the live file.
- **Schema version:** 1 (`migrate.latest("fr")`)
- **Migrations:**
  - Version 1: Baseline (the store has carried version 1 since it was introduced)

### `meta`

Facts about the corpus and its last sync, as key and value (keys below).

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `value` | TEXT |  |  |

### `documents`

One row per Federal Register document, with the API record verbatim in `raw_json`.

| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `document_number` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `type` | TEXT |  |  |
| `title` | TEXT | required |  |
| `abstract` | TEXT |  |  |
| `action` | TEXT |  |  |
| `dates` | TEXT |  |  |

| `publication_date` | TEXT |  |  |
| `effective_on` | TEXT |  |  |
| `comments_close_on` | TEXT |  |  |
| `signing_date` | TEXT |  |  |
| `cfr_references_json` | TEXT | required, default `'[]'` |  |
| `docket_ids_json` | TEXT | required, default `'[]'` |  |
| `rins_json` | TEXT | required, default `'[]'` |  |
| `citation` | TEXT |  | '91 FR 69092' |
| `volume` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `start_page` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `end_page` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `page_length` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `html_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `pdf_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `full_text_xml_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `body_html_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `raw_text_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `raw_json` | TEXT | required |  |

### `document_bodies`

Full text, fetched on demand: the payload as served, its plain text and its hash.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `document_number` | TEXT | primary key, references `documents.document_number` (on delete cascade) |  |
| `format` | TEXT | required | 'xml' \| 'html' |
| `content` | TEXT | required | as served (xml) or sanitized (html) |
| `text` | TEXT | required |  |
| `sha256` | TEXT | required | of the bytes as served |
| `byte_len` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `source_url` | TEXT | required |  |
| `fetched_at` | TEXT | required |  |

### `document_cfr`

Which CFR title, part and section each document touches, and where the link came from.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `document_number` | TEXT | primary key, part 1 of 5, required, references `documents.document_number` (on delete cascade) |  |
| `title` | INTEGER | primary key, part 2 of 5, required |  |
| `part` | TEXT | primary key, part 3 of 5, required |  |

The date ranges that have been fetched, per scope (`title` 0 = every document).

| `start` | TEXT | primary key, part 2 of 3, required |  |

The chunks a full build has finished, so an interrupted build resumes.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `title` | INTEGER | primary key, part 1 of 3, required |  |
| `start` | TEXT | primary key, part 2 of 3, required |  |
| `end` | TEXT | primary key, part 3 of 3, required |  |
| `docs` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `done_at` | TEXT | required |  |

### `documents_fts` (FTS5)

Full-text index over title, abstract, action and body (rowid = the `documents` rowid).

- **Columns:** `title`, `abstract`, `action`, `body`
- **tokenize:** `porter unicode61`

### Meta keys (`meta`)

| Key | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `source` | Where the documents come from (the Federal Register API). |
| `schema` | The schema version as text; `PRAGMA user_version` is the one that counts. |
| `built_at` | When the full build finished. |
| `build_started_at` | When the full build started. |
| `updated_at` | When the corpus was last updated. |
| `window_start` | First publication date collected. |
| `window_end` | Last publication date collected. |
| `titles` | JSON list of the scopes collected (`0` = every document, else CFR titles). |
| `filters` | JSON of the agency, type and CFR-title filters in force. |
| `doc_count` | Rows in `documents`. |
| `last_publication_date` | The newest publication date held. |
| `pending_build` | JSON of the build in progress; only in the staging file. |
| `last_ok_at` | When the last sync succeeded. |
| `fail_count` | Consecutive failed syncs; drives the retry backoff. `0` after a success. |
| `last_error` | The last failure, in a sentence; empty after a success. |
| `last_error_at` | When the last failure happened. |

## Newsroom: `osha_news.sqlite3`

The newsroom feed: recent Federal Register documents, Public Inspection filings and DOL enforcement records, with enriched inspection case files. A cache of public data.

- **Built by:** Created on first use and filled by the background news worker.
- **Written:** Also written between builds: a migration runs in one transaction on the live file.
- **Schema version:** 4 (`migrate.latest("news")`)
- **Migrations:** the store's own module brings older layouts up to version 4; numbered migrations start at 5 (none yet).

### `articles`

One row per news item, whatever its source.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `guid` | TEXT | primary key | "fr:2026-17726" (published or PI), "dol-insp:306953084" |
| `source` | TEXT | required | federal_register \| federal_register_pi \| dol_osha |
| `agency` | TEXT | required |  |
| `category` | TEXT | required | rules \| rulemaking \| notices \| public_inspection \| enforcement |
| `doc_type` | TEXT |  |  |
| `title` | TEXT | required |  |
| `link` | TEXT | required |  |
| `pdf_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `citation` | TEXT |  | "91 FR 55744" |
| `action` | TEXT |  | "Final rule." |
| `effective_on` | TEXT |  | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `comments_close_on` | TEXT |  | YYYY-MM-DD (proposed rules) |
| `scheduled_on` | TEXT |  | YYYY-MM-DD (PI: when it will publish) |
| `published_at` | TEXT | required | YYYY-MM-DD, always (sort key) |
| `description` | TEXT | required, default `''` |  |
| `docket_ids` | TEXT | required, default `'[]'` |  |
| `company` | TEXT |  |  |
| `city` | TEXT |  |  |
| `state` | TEXT |  |  |
| `naics` | TEXT |  |  |
| `penalty_usd` | REAL |  |  |

| `general_duty` | INTEGER | required, default `0` | count of 5(a)(1) citations |
| `unmapped_standards` | INTEGER | required, default `0` | cited standards with no CFR mapping (state plans) |

## U.S. Constitution: `constitution.sqlite3`

The U.S. Constitution by article, section and amendment, with the House Manual's annotations kept apart from the text.

- **Built by:** `python -m app.constitution`. A build replaces the whole file.
- **Written:** Also written between builds: a migration runs in one transaction on the live file.
- **Schema version:** 1 (`migrate.latest("constitution")`)
- **Migrations:**
  - Version 1: Adopt schema versions

### `meta`

Facts about the build, as key and value (keys below).

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `value` | TEXT |  |  |

### `units`

One row per reading unit: the preamble, an article section, an article, an amendment or an amendment section.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `ord` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `kind` | TEXT | required |  |
| `article` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `amendment` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `section` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `label` | TEXT | required |  |
| `text` | TEXT | required |  |
| `note_count` | INTEGER | required, default `0` |  |

### `notes`

The House Manual's annotations for a unit, in order.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | INTEGER | primary key |  |
| `unit_id` | TEXT | required |  |
| `ord` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `text` | TEXT | required |  |

### `units_fts` (FTS5)

Full-text index over `units` (`id` joins back to it).

- **Columns:** `id` (stored, not searched), `label`, `text`
- **tokenize:** `porter unicode61`

### `notes_fts` (FTS5)

Full-text index over `notes` (`unit_id` joins to `units`).

- **Columns:** `unit_id` (stored, not searched), `text`
- **tokenize:** `porter unicode61`

### Meta keys (`meta`)

| Key | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `source` | Where the text comes from (GovInfo bulk data, the House Rules and Manual). |
| `edition` | The House Manual edition, such as `HMAN-118`. |
| `congress` | That edition's Congress. |
| `source_url` | The zip that was downloaded. |

## Public Laws: `plaw.sqlite3`

Public and private laws from the 113th Congress on, as USLM XML, with their links into the U.S. Code.

- **Built by:** `python -m app.plaw` (resumable; staged in `plaw.sqlite3.tmp`), then updated in place.
- **Written:** Also written between builds: a migration runs in one transaction on the live file.
- **Schema version:** 1 (`migrate.latest("plaw")`)
- **Migrations:**
  - Version 1: Adopt schema versions

### `meta`

Facts about the corpus and its last sync, as key and value (keys below).

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `value` | TEXT |  |  |

### `laws`

One row per law; the USLM XML is zlib-compressed in `xml_z`, with its hash and length.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `congress` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `law_type` | TEXT | required |  |
| `number` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `citation` | TEXT |  |  |
| `statute` | TEXT |  |  |
| `title` | TEXT |  |  |
| `approved_date` | TEXT |  |  |
| `bill` | TEXT |  |  |
| `text` | TEXT | required |  |
| `xml_z` | BLOB | required |  |
| `sha256` | TEXT | required |  |
| `byte_len` | INTEGER | required |  |
| `source_url` | TEXT | required |  |
| `fetched_at` | TEXT | required |  |

- **Index** `laws_by_congress`: congress, law_type, number

### `law_usc`

A law's links into the U.S. Code: `reference`, `codified` or `note`.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `law_id` | TEXT | primary key, part 1 of 4, required |  |
| `title` | INTEGER | primary key, part 2 of 4, required |  |
| `section` | TEXT | primary key, part 3 of 4, required |  |
| `kind` | TEXT | primary key, part 4 of 4, required |  |

- **Index** `law_usc_by_section`: title, section

### `build_chunks`

The (congress, type) chunks a build has finished, so an interrupted build resumes.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `congress` | INTEGER | primary key, part 1 of 2 |  |
| `law_type` | TEXT | primary key, part 2 of 2 |  |
| `laws` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `zip_sha256` | TEXT |  |  |
| `source_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `done_at` | TEXT |  |  |

### `laws_fts` (FTS5)

Full-text index over `laws` (`id` joins back to it).

- **Columns:** `id` (stored, not searched), `title`, `text`
- **tokenize:** `porter unicode61`

### Meta keys (`meta`)

| Key | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `source` | Where the laws come from (GovInfo bulk data). |
| `scope` | JSON `{congresses, types, follow}`: what was asked for. |
| `latest_congress` | The newest Congress GovInfo listed at the last sync. |
| `built_at` | When the full build finished. |
| `build_started_at` | When the full build started. |
| `updated_at` | When the corpus was last updated. |
| `law_count` | Rows in `laws`. |
| `usc_link_count` | Rows in `law_usc`. |
| `pending_build` | JSON of the build in progress; only in the staging file. |
| `last_ok_at` | When the last sync succeeded. |
| `fail_count` | Consecutive failed syncs; drives the retry backoff. `0` after a success. |
| `last_error` | The last failure, in a sentence; empty after a success. |
| `last_error_at` | When the last failure happened. |

## Unified Agenda: `agenda.sqlite3`

The Unified Agenda of regulatory actions: one row per rule (RIN) per edition.

- **Built by:** `python -m app.agenda` (resumable; staged in `agenda.sqlite3.tmp`), then updated in place.
- **Written:** Also written between builds: a migration runs in one transaction on the live file.
- **Schema version:** 1 (`migrate.latest("agenda")`)
- **Migrations:**
  - Version 1: Adopt schema versions

### `meta`

Facts about the corpus and its last sync, as key and value (keys below).

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `value` | TEXT |  |  |

### `entries`

One row per rule (RIN) per edition.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `rin` | TEXT | primary key, part 1 of 2, required |  |
| `edition` | TEXT | primary key, part 2 of 2, required |  |
| `agency_code` | TEXT |  |  |
| `agency` | TEXT |  |  |
| `agency_acronym` | TEXT |  |  |
| `parent_code` | TEXT |  |  |
| `parent` | TEXT |  |  |
| `parent_acronym` | TEXT |  |  |
| `title` | TEXT | required |  |
| `abstract` | TEXT |  |  |
| `stage` | TEXT |  |  |
| `priority` | TEXT |  |  |
| `major` | TEXT |  |  |
| `rin_status` | TEXT |  |  |
| `rplan` | TEXT |  |  |
| `cfr_json` | TEXT |  |  |
| `authority_json` | TEXT |  |  |
| `timetable_json` | TEXT |  |  |
| `related_json` | TEXT |  |  |
| `further_info_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `comment_url` | TEXT |  |  |

- **Index** `entries_by_edition`: edition, parent_code, stage

### `editions`

One row per Agenda edition downloaded, with its hash and source URL.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `edition` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `title` | TEXT |  |  |
| `entries` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `sha256` | TEXT |  |  |
| `byte_len` | INTEGER |  |  |
| `source_url` | TEXT |  |  |
| `run_date` | TEXT |  |  |

The editions a build has finished, so an interrupted build resumes.

## Source selection: `sources.sqlite3`

The reader's saved choice of data sources and their saved templates. The one store that holds the reader's own settings rather than public data.

- **Built by:** Created the first time a selection or template is saved.
- **Written:** Also written between builds: a migration runs in one transaction on the live file.
- **Schema version:** 1 (`migrate.latest("sources")`)
- **Migrations:**
  - Version 1: Baseline (the store has carried version 1 since it was introduced)

### `settings`

Key and JSON value. The one key in use is `selection`: the saved source selection.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `key` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `value` | TEXT | required |  |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | required |  |

### `templates`

The reader's saved selection templates.

| Column | Type | Rules | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | TEXT | primary key |  |
| `name` | TEXT | required |  |
| `description` | TEXT | required, default `''` |  |
| `selection` | TEXT | required |  |
| `created_at` | TEXT | required |  |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | required |  |
